title: Putting Skills into Practice: Integrated Workshop
summary: Brings the programme together in a simulated supervisory exercise in which participants analyse information, meet a firm and present their findings.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Brings the programme together in a simulated supervisory exercise in which participants analyse information, meet a firm and present their findings.
Learning Objectives: Combine analysis, meeting, challenge and writing skills in a realistic scenario
Produce a clear written output from the exercise
Reflect on strengths and set personal development priorities
Syllabus: Case briefing and analysis of firm information
Mock firm meeting with challenge and note-taking
Drafting a follow-up letter and short committee paper
Workshop: presentations, peer feedback and personal development plans
Intended Audience: New joiners and developing staff in supervisory, authorisation, policy and enforcement roles
Staff recently promoted into case-handling roles who want to strengthen core skills
Line managers seeking a common standard of professional practice for their teams
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior experience is required. The programme is suitable for staff in their first years at the authority as well as those wishing to refresh core skills.
Core Reading: IMF (2010), The Making of Good Supervision: Learning to Say "No" (Staff Position Note SPN/10/08)
IMF (2023), Good Supervision: Lessons from the Field (Working Paper WP/23/181)
FSB (2014), Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture: A Framework for Assessing Risk Culture
